lsystems.name: L-Systems: Rules Grow Structure
lsystems.truth: A sentence can become a forest. Grammar is generative.
lsystems.qfep_connection: L-systems sit at the edge between deterministic rules (F) and emergent complexity (E). Simple rewriting rules produce infinite variation. The lambda parameter is iteration count â€” each generation pushes further toward the edge.

Start in the grammar lab, watch growth unfold, formalize the rules, build cities, compete for space, and finally watch the world come alive.

artifact_groups.rationale: Interactive pipeline: editor, tree output, visible string expansion, and visual anchor. Axiom rewriting producing organic structure.
Four tree artifacts: animated growth, context-sensitive branching, static comparison, and continuous parameter tweaking. Same axiom, different context, different trees.
3D Hilbert curve overhead and floor gallery of Hilbert/Peano/Moore curves. Formal grammar generating paths that visit every point.
City and dungeon generation using L-system rules. Same grammar yields different spatial results when turtle interpretation changes.
Competing growth systems (forest + coral) where ecology emerges from local grammar interactions within shared constraints.
Grammar becomes world: player designs tree DNA (sculptor), coral grows, terrain follows branching logic. Rules-that-make-trees become rules-that-make-worlds.
Introduces L-system concept with interactive editor and basic tree. First map, beginner-friendly.
Builds on intro with animated growth and context-sensitive variation. Four tree artifacts showing generational progression.
Formal grammar meets space-filling curves. Two focused artifacts showing rules visiting every point.
Grammar beyond biology. City and dungeon generation show L-systems as architectural tools.
Multiple growth systems competing for space. Ecology emerges from grammar interactions.
Synthesis map with callbacks to tree (intro), coral (integration), plus genetic sculptor bridging to evolution. Grammar becomes biology.
